column1: Ukraine's request for weapons from Russia is part of a broader NATO plan to arm Ukraine with up to 1,000 armoured personnel carriers, more than doubling the number of Russian combat vehicles and two-thirds of the Russian warplanes, as its own air force makes a bigger and more agile contribution to the fight against the Islamic State group, which has been fighting there for months.

The request for arms comes after the European Union agreed on a $1.2bn defence budget for 2014, with the European Union and Russia on a joint defence spending plan. With the aid of Russian arms suppliers, it is said, Ukraine will now be able to deploy its air force, and deploy an additional 5,000 troops in the next three years.
Ukraine was due to meet Russian defence minister Avigdor Liberman on Friday to discuss the request and a list of suppliers.

The EU's defence ministers, including Defence Minister Antoni Macierewicz, also met Russian defence expert Mikhail Yatsenyuk, who said that Russia's arms deal with Russia "is a step in the right direction", adding that the EU would try to find other supplies in order to develop their influence.
On Monday, the EU agreed on the supply of weapons to Ukraine for air-launched anti-tank missiles. The agreement was approved by EU defence ministers when both sides agreed on the issue on Tuesday.
For its part, the Russian defence ministry said the agreement would provide a "long-term solution" to the Ukrainian military's "long-term military situation".

We are very pleased that the Russian military has fulfilled its commitments, said Sergey Konstantinov, the Russian defence ministry spokesman. "We are ready to contribute to the fight against the Islamic State group in Syria and Iraq. Russia is in a position to provide the necessary military equipment and equipment to Ukraine."
The Russian military's new year offensive has seen it win more than 25,000 troops, including helicopters, tanks and SU-25 fighters, and has helped it recapture territory from the Islamic State group.
